candidates.title: Show HN: Trifle – Open-source analytics that stores answers, not events
candidates.excerpt:
Trifle is an open-source time-series analytics library that aggregates nested counters instead of storing raw events. All in the database you already have. After rebuilding it twice over 10 years, it now tracks ~1B events a day at my day job.

candidates.discovered_via: github_query:is:issue is:open (bounty OR reward OR paid OR stipend) archived:false
candidates.excerpt: ## 📝 Description When the reverse proxy attempts to retry a failed upstream request, the backend receives an empty request body. In Go, the `http.Request.Body` is an `io.ReadCloser` stream. Once the reverse proxy reads the body to transmit it to the first upstream server, the stream is fully consumed (reaching `EOF`). If that initial connection fails or returns a retryable error, subsequent retry attempts reuse the same `http.Request` object, but the `Body` stream is now empty. As a result, retried requests are dispatched with a content length of 0 or an empty body, causing upstream validation failures. ## 🎯 Acceptance Criteria - [ ] The reverse proxy must preserve and replay the original request body for all retry attempts. - [ ] If the request body is read into memory for retries, there must be a configurable limit on the maximum body size to prevent Out-Of-Memory (OOM) vulnerabilities
